excerpt: Prisma makes the open-source Prisma ORM for TypeScript plus Prisma Postgres and Prisma Compute hosting. Free plan, paid plans from $10 a month. Funding and alternatives.
content:
Prisma is a developer tools company best known for Prisma ORM, an open-source object-relational mapper for Node.js and TypeScript. Developers describe their data model in a schema file, and Prisma generates a type-safe client for querying the database, plus tools for schema migrations. The company has since added hosted products: Prisma Postgres, a managed PostgreSQL database, and Prisma Compute, which its website says hosts TypeScript apps (Node.js, Bun or Next.js) next to the database and has been generally available since August 2026. Its homepage now pitches it as agent infrastructure for TypeScript and notes that any Postgres client works, so the ORM is optional.

Prisma started out as a Berlin and San Francisco startup building a GraphQL data layer. In May 2018 TechCrunch reported a $4.5 million seed round led by Kleiner Perkins and said cofounder and CEO Johannes Schickling planned to grow the team and open a San Francisco office; Kleiner Perkins announced the same round. The company later shifted from GraphQL to the ORM and hosted database products it sells today, and its website advertises an AI developer conference in San Francisco on 26 October 2026.

Prisma publishes usage-based prices. The Free plan costs $0 and includes 1 million Compute requests and 200,000 Postgres operations a month. Starter is $10 a month, Pro $49 a month and Business $129 a month, each with larger included usage and per-unit charges above it. The ORM itself remains free and open source.

We have not used Prisma for this page. It brings together Prisma's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.

alternatives.intro: Other tools and companies often compared with Prisma. We have not compared them hands-on; check each one's own site for current prices.

items.name: Drizzle ORM
items.difference: SQL-like, lighter-weight alternative popular with TypeScript developers.

items.name: Neon
items.difference: Managed Postgres with branching; pairs with any ORM.

items.name: Supabase
items.difference: Postgres with auth, storage and APIs built in.

faq.a: Prisma ORM is free and open source. Hosted Prisma Postgres and Compute have a free plan; paid plans start at $10 a month.
Johannes Schickling is a cofounder; TechCrunch described him as CEO when Prisma raised its 2018 seed round.

faq.q: Do I have to use Prisma ORM with Prisma Postgres?
faq.a: No. Prisma's homepage says any Postgres client works and the ORM is optional.
